question: A previously healthy 24-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-day history of painful rash after spending several hours in the sun. Skin examination shows well-demarcated areas of erythema with some scaling on the face, chest, upper back, and arms. The affected areas are hot and sensitive to touch. The oral mucosa appears normal. Which of the following is the most likely underlying mechanism of this patient's skin findings?

options.opa: Vascular endothelial cell injury in the superficial dermis
options.opb: Immune complex deposits at the dermoepidermal junction
options.opc: Mast cell activation in the superficial dermis
options.opd: Apoptosis of keratinocytes in the epidermis
options.ope: T-cell-mediated inflammatory reaction in the dermis

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Mast cell activation in the superficial dermis -> Release of histamine and other inflammatory mediators -> Vasodilation and increased vascular permeability -> Erythema, heat, and sensitivity to touch -> 80%
analysis: The patient's presentation with a painful rash after sun exposure is suggestive of sunburn, which is caused by ultraviolet (UV) radiation-induced damage to the skin. The most likely underlying mechanism in this case is vascular endothelial cell injury in the superficial dermis due to UV radiation exposure.
